decisions.title: Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
decisions.content:
Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
The API reads the token from the Authorization header. It does not set or read any cookie.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Cookie transport would need CSRF protection that this API does not have (ADR-5). Invented for this demo.

decisions.title: PostgreSQL is the data store and MongoDB was not chosen.
decisions.content:
PostgreSQL is the data store and MongoDB was not chosen.
Articles, tags and favorites are stored in PostgreSQL tables joined by foreign keys.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The data is relational, and the DBA team supports only PostgreSQL (ADR-3). Invented for this demo.

decisions.title: bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
decisions.content:
bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
No custom rounds value is set on the password context, so passlib's default applies.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Load test LT-9 put the login endpoint at a p95 of 240 ms with the default factor. One step higher pushed it past the 300 ms login budget. Invented for this demo.

decisions.title: Deleted articles and comments are removed from the database, with no soft-delete flag.
decisions.content:
Deleted articles and comments are removed from the database, with no soft-delete flag.
Deleting an article or a comment runs a SQL DELETE. No deleted_at column exists.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Legal review LR-77 requires that content its author deleted is gone from live storage within 24 hours. A deleted_at column was rejected because the rows would stay in the table. Invented for this demo.

decisions.title: Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.
decisions.content:
Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.
The API issues a single access token that is valid for one week and has no refresh endpoint. A client that needs a new token logs in again.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Security review SR-2025-14 of the pilot found that a stored refresh token let a stolen browser profile keep access for months. The team chose a one-week access token and no refresh token, so a stolen token expires on its own. Invented for this demo.

decisions.title: A separately stored per-user salt is prepended to the password before hashing.
decisions.content:
UserInDB.change_password generates a salt, stores it in the salt column, and hashes salt + password. check_password must prepend the same salt, so the salt column and the hash must change together.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24

decisions.title: Cross-origin calls are allowed from the origins in allowed_hosts, which default to every origin.
decisions.content:
The CORS middleware reads allowed_hosts from the settings. The default list holds a single wildcard entry.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:31

decisions.title: Access tokens are signed with the HS256 algorithm using one shared secret key.
decisions.content:
Tokens are JWTs signed and verified with HS256. The secret comes from the application settings.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

decisions.title: The Authorization header must use the prefix Token, not Bearer.
decisions.content:
AppSettings sets jwt_token_prefix to Token. _get_authorization_header splits the header on a space and rejects any prefix that does not match this setting.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

decisions.title: Access tokens expire after one week and there is no refresh token.
decisions.content:
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 60 * 24 * 7 and create_access_token_for_user uses it as the expiry delta. No refresh or revocation mechanism exists in the code.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

decisions.title: Creating a tag that already exists is ignored by the insert statement.
decisions.content:
The tag insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so saving an article with a known tag adds no new tag row.
Source: app/app/db/queries/sql/tags.sql:9

decisions.title: Only an article's author, matched by username, may modify the article.
decisions.content:
The service compares the article author's username with the current user's username. Other users get a refusal.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

decisions.title: Request validation failures return HTTP 422 with an errors list of the validator's error objects.
decisions.content:
A separate handler catches validation errors and answers with the validator's own error list, not the single detail string used for other HTTP errors.
Source: app/app/api/errors/validation_error.py:17

decisions.title: Every access token carries the fixed subject claim access.
decisions.content:
The token payload holds the username plus an expiry and the subject value access, which is a constant in the JWT service.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:10

decisions.title: Deleting a user keeps their articles and sets author_id to NULL.
decisions.content:
The articles.author_id foreign key uses ondelete SET NULL and is nullable, while comments, favorites and follows use CASCADE. Articles can therefore exist without an author.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108

decisions.title: Only the author may update or delete an article, checked by comparing usernames.
decisions.content:
check_user_can_modify_article compares the article author username with the current user username. check_article_modification_permissions raises 403 when they differ and guards the PUT and DELETE routes.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

decisions.title: Login returns the same error for an unknown email and a wrong password.
decisions.content:
The login route builds one wrong_login_error and raises it both when the email lookup fails and when check_password fails. Both cases return 400 with INCORRECT_LOGIN_INPUT.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:28

decisions.title: The token identifies the user by username, not by user id.
decisions.content:
create_access_token_for_user puts only the username in the payload, and _get_current_user looks the user up by that username. Renaming a user makes old tokens fail, so the update-user route issues a new token.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

decisions.title: Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
decisions.content:
Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
The API reads the token from the Authorization header. It does not set or read any cookie.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Cookie transport would need CSRF protection that this API does not have (ADR-5). Invented for this demo.

decisions.content:

Reason: The DBA team reviews every query. A SQL file can be reviewed in a pull request and ORM output cannot (ADR-4). Invented for this demo.

The create route builds the slug from the title and checks whether an article with that slug exists. If it does, the route raises a 400 error and does not add a numeric suffix.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65

decisions.title: Cross-origin calls are allowed from the origins in allowed_hosts, which default to every origin.
decisions.content:
The CORS middleware reads allowed_hosts from the settings. The default list holds a single wildcard entry.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:31

decisions.title: Access tokens are signed with the HS256 algorithm using one shared secret key.
decisions.content:
Tokens are JWTs signed and verified with HS256. The secret comes from the application settings.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

decisions.title: Updating an article title regenerates its slug, so its URL changes.
decisions.content:
update_article_by_slug recomputes the slug from the new title when a title is given and passes it to the repository as new_slug. Unlike creation, this path does not check for an existing slug first.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:100

decisions.title: The Authorization header must use the prefix Token, not Bearer.
decisions.content:
AppSettings sets jwt_token_prefix to Token. _get_authorization_header splits the header on a space and rejects any prefix that does not match this setting.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

decisions.title: Access tokens expire after one week and there is no refresh token.
decisions.content:
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 60 * 24 * 7 and create_access_token_for_user uses it as the expiry delta. No refresh or revocation mechanism exists in the code.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

decisions.title: Creating a tag that already exists is ignored by the insert statement.
decisions.content:
The tag insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so saving an article with a known tag adds no new tag row.
Source: app/app/db/queries/sql/tags.sql:9

decisions.title: The database pool is fixed at 10 connections through min_connection_count and max_connection_count.
decisions.content:
Both pool bounds default to 10 in the application settings, and the pool is created with those two values at start-up.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:22

decisions.title: Only an article's author, matched by username, may modify the article.
decisions.content:
The service compares the article author's username with the current user's username. Other users get a refusal.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

decisions.title: Registering with a username or email that is already taken is answered with HTTP 400.
decisions.content:
The register route checks the username first and the email second. Each taken value raises a 400 error with its own message from the strings module.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:70

decisions.title: Request validation failures return HTTP 422 with an errors list of the validator's error objects.
decisions.content:
A separate handler catches validation errors and answers with the validator's own error list, not the single detail string used for other HTTP errors.
Source: app/app/api/errors/validation_error.py:17

decisions.title: Each user gets a random salt created with bcrypt.gensalt.
decisions.content:
A helper returns a fresh bcrypt salt as text. The user row stores the salt next to the hashed password.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:8

decisions.title: Every access token carries the fixed subject claim access.
decisions.content:
The token payload holds the username plus an expiry and the subject value access, which is a constant in the JWT service.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:10

decisions.title: API models use camelCase JSON aliases generated from snake_case field names.
decisions.content:
RWModel sets alias_generator to convert_field_to_camel_case and allows population by field name. Renaming a Python field changes the public JSON key.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21

decisions.title: Database access uses raw SQL files loaded with aiosql on asyncpg, not an ORM.
decisions.content:
queries.py loads every .sql file in app/db/queries/sql with the asyncpg adapter, and repositories call these named queries. Only filter_articles builds SQL dynamically with pypika.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5

decisions.title: updated_at is maintained by a Postgres trigger, not by application code.
decisions.content:
The migration creates the plpgsql function update_updated_at_column and BEFORE UPDATE triggers on users, articles and commentaries that set updated_at to now().
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27

decisions.title: Deleting a user keeps their articles and sets author_id to NULL.
decisions.content:
The articles.author_id foreign key uses ondelete SET NULL and is nullable, while comments, favorites and follows use CASCADE. Articles can therefore exist without an author.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108

decisions.title: Only the author may update or delete an article, checked by comparing usernames.
decisions.content:
check_user_can_modify_article compares the article author username with the current user username. check_article_modification_permissions raises 403 when they differ and guards the PUT and DELETE routes.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

decisions.title: Login returns the same error for an unknown email and a wrong password.
decisions.content:
The login route builds one wrong_login_error and raises it both when the email lookup fails and when check_password fails. Both cases return 400 with INCORRECT_LOGIN_INPUT.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:28

decisions.title: The token identifies the user by username, not by user id.
decisions.content:
create_access_token_for_user puts only the username in the payload, and _get_current_user looks the user up by that username. Renaming a user makes old tokens fail, so the update-user route issues a new token.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

decisions.title: Datetimes are serialized as UTC ISO strings ending in Z.
decisions.content:
convert_datetime_to_realworld forces the UTC timezone and replaces +00:00 with Z; RWModel registers it as the datetime JSON encoder. It overwrites any existing tzinfo rather than converting it.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:7

decisions.title: Article lists default to 20 items and have no upper limit.
decisions.content:
DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT is 20 and the limit query parameter is only constrained by ge=1, with no maximum. A client can request any page size.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:8

decisions.title: Bad tokens, wrong prefixes and unknown users are answered with 403, not 401.
decisions.content:
_get_authorization_header and _get_current_user raise HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN for a malformed header, a wrong prefix, an undecodable token and a user that no longer exists. Clients see 403 for every authentication failure of a present header.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:54
